sub_scenario.family: communicating uncertainty and risk escalation in cross-functional decisions
sub_scenario.one_line: hospital partnership coordinator: request the missing process details

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the referral log and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The partner diary review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I arranged a standard referral in the afternoon when every service had confirmed capacity.
Was the discharge cause still open?
No, the capacity checks were complete.
Someone new shadowed me in the care coordination desk this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the winter surge into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
I did a standard pass over the partner diary records this morning.
Any exceptions in there?
None worth a note.
I corrected a partner contact in the referral log yesterday.
Did that settle a complex escalation?
No, it was an administrative fix.
I archived last cycle's notes on the partner diary and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The daily 15:30 escalation hour is on the partner diary, and the winter-surge staffing grid closes at 16:00.
Are those times movable?
No, both are fixed on the coordination schedule.
A vendor call about the referral log ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the care coordination desk checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the winter surge.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the partner diary records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
I closed a routine winter surge cycle without surprises.
Follow-up needed?
A note for the next cycle, nothing more.
I sketched next week's plan for the winter surge before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the referral log updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
A next-morning multidisciplinary huddle is available at 08:30, and the partner diary lists separate review-only and assignment fields for the office hour.
Are those resources confirmed?
Yes, the huddle slot and both fields appear on the roster.
I compared two options for the partner diary tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the care coordination desk handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
The partnership office asks me to RSVP to its daily 15:30 escalation hour, but its decision authority and record requirements are unspecified. What should I reply?

query: The partnership office asks me to RSVP to its daily 15:30 escalation hour, but its decision authority and record requirements are unspecified. What should I reply?

ev_A.fact: During a complex discharge review, I marked ward notes, family-call status, and transport records as confirmed, pending, or missing on the referral log before the morning coordination call; the team held the referral until the missing call returned.

ev_B.fact: In a complex discharge escalation, I named home nursing as the cause of a delay before separating the ward notes from an unreturned family call, and the team pursued the wrong gap.

E1.fact: The daily 15:30 escalation hour is on the partner diary, and the winter-surge staffing grid closes at 16:00.

E2.fact: A next-morning multidisciplinary huddle is available at 08:30, and the partner diary lists separate review-only and assignment fields for the office hour.

relation_specificity.why_it_does_not_license_C: Those routine tasks establish neither the record-marking contribution nor the reason process details must precede an RSVP.
